question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.14(3)(a), one ground for reprimand, limitation, suspension, or revocation of a license is what?
choice_a: Making a material misstatement in the application for a license, or in any information furnished to the board
choice_b: Being late to a single closing
choice_c: Failing to attend a board meeting
choice_d: Advertising a property using a professional photographer
explanation: 452.14(3)(a) makes it grounds for discipline that the licensee has made a material misstatement in the application for a license, or in any information furnished to the board.

question: Under 452.14(3)(b), a licensee is subject to discipline for making what kind of misrepresentation?
choice_a: Any misrepresentation, no matter how minor or harmless
choice_b: Any substantial misrepresentation with reference to a transaction injurious to a party
choice_c: A misrepresentation made only to another licensee
choice_d: A misrepresentation corrected before closing
explanation: 452.14(3)(b) lists as a ground for discipline having made any substantial misrepresentation with reference to a transaction injurious to a party.

question: Per 452.14(3)(c), what kind of promise made by a licensee is grounds for discipline?
choice_a: A promise to hold an open house
choice_b: A promise to respond to inquiries within 24 hours
choice_c: A false promise of a character such as to influence, persuade, or induce a party
choice_d: A promise to lower the licensee's commission
explanation: 452.14(3)(c) makes it a ground for discipline to have made false promises of a character such as to influence, persuade, or induce a party.

question: Under 452.14(3)(d), discipline may be based on what pattern of conduct?
choice_a: A single, isolated instance of a typographical error in a listing
choice_b: Advertising the same property twice in one week
choice_c: Declining a below-market offer
choice_d: A continued and flagrant course of misrepresentation, or making false promises through real estate licensees, employees, advertising, or otherwise
explanation: 452.14(3)(d) provides that pursuing a continued and flagrant course of misrepresentation, or making false promises through real estate licensees, employees, advertising, or otherwise, is grounds for discipline.

question: Per 452.14(3)(f), it is grounds for discipline for a licensee to accept a commission or valuable consideration from whom?
choice_a: Any person except the firm with which the licensee is associated, for acts or services performed under ch. 452
choice_b: The licensee's own client, when disclosed in writing
choice_c: The board, as a licensing fee
choice_d: A title company, for referring a title search
explanation: 452.14(3)(f) makes it grounds for discipline to have accepted a commission or valuable consideration for the performance of any act specified in ch. 452 from any person except the firm with which the licensee is associated.

question: Under 452.14(3)(g), what conduct regarding representing a firm is grounds for discipline?
choice_a: Representing more than one firm during the licensee's career
choice_b: Representing, or attempting to represent, a firm without the express knowledge and consent of that firm
choice_c: Representing a firm located outside Wisconsin
choice_d: Representing a firm at a real estate conference
explanation: 452.14(3)(g) makes it grounds for discipline to have represented, or attempted to represent, a real estate firm other than the licensee's employer or firm, without the express knowledge and consent of the licensee's employer or firm.

question: Per 452.14(3)(h), a licensee is subject to discipline for failing to do what within a reasonable time?
choice_a: Renew the licensee's continuing education credits
choice_b: Update the multiple listing service photos
choice_c: Account for or remit any moneys coming into the licensee's possession that belong to others
choice_d: Respond to a marketing survey
explanation: 452.14(3)(h) makes it grounds for discipline to have failed, within a reasonable time, to account for or remit any moneys coming into the licensee's possession that belong to others.

question: Under 452.14(3)(i), a licensee may be disciplined for having demonstrated what?
choice_a: An unusually low number of closed transactions in a calendar year
choice_b: A preference for residential over commercial listings
choice_c: Limited experience with a particular neighborhood
choice_d: Incompetency to act as a broker or salesperson in a manner that safeguards the interests of the public
explanation: 452.14(3)(i) makes it grounds for discipline to have demonstrated incompetency to act as a broker or salesperson in such a manner as to safeguard the interests of the public.

question: Per 452.14(3)(im), discipline may be based on violating which other statute, which governs disclosures by real property wholesalers?
choice_a: Section 710.13(2)
choice_b: Section 100.20
choice_c: Section 138.052
choice_d: Section 706.02
explanation: 452.14(3)(im) makes violating s. 710.13(2) a ground for discipline; that statute requires a real property wholesaler to give written notice of wholesaler status to the seller before entering a purchase agreement, and to a third-party assignee before assigning the wholesaler's contract rights.

question: Under 452.14(3)(j), what is grounds for discipline regarding commissions paid to others?
choice_a: Paying a referral fee to a licensed out-of-state broker under a written agreement
choice_b: Paying or offering to pay a commission or valuable consideration to any person for acts or services performed in violation of ch. 452
choice_c: Paying a commission to the licensee's own firm
choice_d: Paying for a home warranty on behalf of a buyer
explanation: 452.14(3)(j) makes it grounds for discipline to have paid or offered to pay a commission or valuable consideration to any person for acts or services performed in violation of ch. 452.

question: Per 452.14(3)(jm), a licensee may be disciplined for intentionally encouraging or discouraging a person from purchasing or renting real estate on what basis?
choice_a: The person's stated budget
choice_b: The person's preferred closing date
choice_c: Race, in violation of steering-type conduct governed by this paragraph
choice_d: The person's choice of lender
explanation: 452.14(3)(jm) makes it grounds for discipline to have intentionally encouraged or discouraged any person from purchasing or renting real estate on the basis of the racial composition of a neighborhood -- classic real-estate 'steering.'

question: Under 452.14(3)(k), a licensee is subject to discipline for being guilty of what catch-all category of conduct?
choice_a: Only conduct that has already resulted in a civil lawsuit
choice_b: Only conduct occurring during business hours
choice_c: Only conduct that also violates a separate criminal statute
choice_d: Any other conduct, whether of the same or a different character than specified elsewhere in the paragraph, that constitutes improper, fraudulent, or dishonest dealing
explanation: 452.14(3)(k) is a catch-all: a licensee may be disciplined for being guilty of any other conduct, whether of the same or a different character than the conduct specified elsewhere in the subsection, that constitutes improper, fraudulent, or dishonest dealing.

question: Per 452.14(3)(L), what broad category of violation is separately listed as a ground for discipline?
choice_a: Violating any provision of ch. 452 or any rule promulgated under the chapter
choice_b: Violating a local municipal noise ordinance
choice_c: Violating a homeowners' association bylaw
choice_d: Violating a nondisclosure agreement with a former employer
explanation: 452.14(3)(L) makes it grounds for discipline to have violated any provision of ch. 452 or any rule promulgated under the chapter.

question: Under 452.14(3)(m), a licensee may be disciplined for failing to do what regarding forms?
choice_a: Print forms in a particular font
choice_b: Use the forms approved under s. 452.05(1)(b)
choice_c: File copies of forms with the county recorder
choice_d: Retype forms rather than using fillable PDFs
explanation: 452.14(3)(m) makes it grounds for discipline to have failed to use the forms approved under s. 452.05(1)(b).

question: Under 452.14(3)(n), treating a person unequally on which of the following bases is grounds for discipline?
choice_a: Price range of the property the person can afford
choice_b: Whether the person is represented by an attorney
choice_c: Sex, race, color, handicap, national origin, ancestry, marital status, lawful source of income, or status as a victim of domestic abuse, sexual assault, or stalking
choice_d: The person's preferred method of contact
explanation: 452.14(3)(n) makes it grounds for discipline to have treated any person unequally solely because of sex, race, color, handicap, national origin, ancestry, marital status, lawful source of income, or status as a victim of domestic abuse, sexual assault, or stalking as defined in s. 106.50(1m)(u).

question: Per 452.14(3)(o), discipline may be based on violating s. 452.25(2)(a) or failing to do what?
choice_a: Renew a listing agreement in a timely manner
choice_b: Attend the licensee's own disciplinary hearing
choice_c: File a change-of-address form
choice_d: Pay any forfeiture assessed by the board
explanation: 452.14(3)(o) makes it grounds for discipline to have violated s. 452.25(2)(a) (which, hedge: exact cross-referenced provisions unpinned -- generally bars intentionally submitting false information on a board-created form) or to have failed to pay any forfeiture assessed by the board.
source_note: Wis. Stat. 452.14(3)(o); 452.25(2)(a) -- hedge: precise cross-reference wording of 452.25(2)(a) not independently pinned

question: Under 452.14(3)(p), a conviction is grounds for discipline when the circumstances of the offense are what?
choice_a: Substantially related to the circumstances of the practice of a broker or salesperson, subject to the limitations of ss. 111.321, 111.322, and 111.335
choice_b: Of any kind, regardless of relation to real estate practice
choice_c: Only traffic violations
choice_d: Limited to convictions occurring after licensure
explanation: 452.14(3)(p) makes it grounds for discipline to have been convicted of an offense the circumstances of which substantially relate to the circumstances of the practice of a broker or salesperson, subject to the fair-employment limitations in ss. 111.321, 111.322, and 111.335.

question: Under 452.14(1), what triggers a board investigation of a broker or salesperson?
choice_a: Only a signed, notarized written complaint from a former client
choice_b: Credible information, whether from the secretary's motion or the board's own determination, indicating a violation of ch. 452 or its rules
choice_c: Only a referral from a circuit court
choice_d: Only an anonymous tip verified by police
explanation: 452.14(1) allows the board to investigate a broker or salesperson upon the secretary's motion or its own determination when credible information shows a violation of ch. 452 or rules promulgated under it.

question: Per 452.14(2), when the board commences disciplinary proceedings against a licensee associated with a firm, what must the board do regarding that firm?
choice_a: Automatically suspend the firm's registration pending outcome
choice_b: Nothing; firms are not notified of proceedings against associated licensees
choice_c: Notify the firm in writing of the proceedings
choice_d: Publish the firm's name in a newspaper of general circulation
explanation: 452.14(2) requires the board to notify a firm in writing when disciplinary proceedings are commenced against a licensee associated with that firm.

question: Under 452.14(4), when may a business entity licensed as a firm be disciplined based on the acts of a representative?
choice_a: Only if every owner of the entity personally participated
choice_b: Only if the entity has fewer than five licensees
choice_c: Never; entity discipline requires a separate statute
choice_d: When there is sufficient cause because a representative or connected party committed acts that would disqualify an individual from licensure
explanation: 452.14(4) provides that a business entity is subject to discipline where there is sufficient cause because a representative of, or person connected with, the entity has committed acts or omissions that would disqualify an individual applicant or licensee from receiving or holding a license.

question: Per 452.14(4m), in addition to license discipline, what other remedies may the board impose for a violation?
choice_a: Forfeitures of up to $5,000 per violation and required completion of additional education or training
choice_b: Immediate criminal referral for every violation, regardless of severity
choice_c: Mandatory dissolution of the licensee's firm
choice_d: Public censure only, with no monetary penalty available
explanation: 452.14(4m) allows the board to assess forfeitures of up to $5,000 per violation and to require completion of education or training beyond standard requirements, in addition to other discipline.

question: Under 452.14(5), if the board revokes or suspends a license, what recourse is available regarding judicial review, and who may represent the board?
choice_a: Only a jury trial in circuit court is available, with no administrative review option
choice_b: A licensee may seek judicial review under ch. 227, and the attorney general may represent the board if requested
choice_c: No judicial review of board discipline is available under Wisconsin law
choice_d: Only the department, never the attorney general, may represent the board
explanation: 452.14(5) provides for judicial review of board decisions under ch. 227, and allows the attorney general to represent the board if requested by the department.

question: Per 452.133(2)(b), a firm's duty to disclose information to its client covers what, and what is expressly excluded?
choice_a: Only information the client specifically asks about in writing
choice_b: Only information relating to the physical condition of the property
choice_c: All information known by the firm that is material to the transaction and not known or discoverable by the client, except confidential information under sub.(1)(d)
choice_d: All firm files without any exceptions
explanation: 452.133(2)(b) is the client-only duty to disclose to the client all information known by the firm that is material to the transaction and not known by, or discoverable by, the client through reasonably vigilant observation, except for information the firm is required to keep confidential under sub.(1)(d).

question: Under 452.133(2)(c), a firm owes its client the duty to fulfill what?
choice_a: Any request the client makes, without exception
choice_b: Only obligations that are also written into the offer to purchase
choice_c: Obligations owed to the other party's firm
choice_d: Any obligation required by the agency agreement and any order of the client within its scope, not inconsistent with another duty under ch. 452 or other law
explanation: 452.133(2)(c) is the duty to fulfill any obligation required by the agency agreement, and any order of the client within the scope of that agreement, that is not inconsistent with another duty the firm has under ch. 452 or any other law.

question: Per 452.133(4m), how do the duties and prohibitions that apply to a firm under sub.(1) through (3) apply to individual licensees associated with that firm?
choice_a: They extend to and are equally binding on the associated licensees and any subagents, to the extent the licensee is actively providing brokerage services to a party
choice_b: They apply only to the firm's broker, never to salespersons
choice_c: They do not apply to individual licensees at all, only to the licensed firm as an entity
choice_d: They apply only after the licensee has been associated with the firm for one year
explanation: 452.133(4m) extends the duties and prohibitions imposed on a firm under the section to the individual licensees associated with the firm and to any subagents, so licensees actively providing brokerage services owe the same duties as the firm.

question: Under 452.133(5), when a firm provides brokerage services without an agency agreement and without acting as a subagent, what is the firm restricted from doing?
choice_a: Communicating with either party to the transaction at all
choice_b: Providing advice that is contrary to the interests of another party to the transaction, unless required by law
choice_c: Accepting any compensation whatsoever for the services provided
choice_d: Preparing any written proposal on behalf of a party
explanation: 452.133(5) provides that a firm providing brokerage services without an agency agreement or a subagency role still owes the sub.(1) duties to parties, but may not give advice contrary to the interests of another party to the transaction unless required by law.

question: Per 452.136(2)(b), when a licensee associated with a firm advertises, under whose name and supervision must the advertising occur?
choice_a: The licensee's own name exclusively, never the firm's
choice_b: A trade name chosen solely by the licensee without firm approval
choice_c: The firm's name, prominently displayed, under the firm's supervision, unless the licensee is engaged in independent practice under s. 452.30(6)
choice_d: The board's name, as the licensing authority
explanation: 452.136(2)(b) requires an associated licensee's advertising to prominently feature the firm's name and be conducted under the firm's supervision, unless the licensee is engaged in independent practice as permitted under s. 452.30(6).

question: Per REEB 24.02, an "adverse fact" is defined generally as what?
choice_a: Any fact that could theoretically influence any buyer, no matter how minor
choice_b: A fact disclosed only in a title commitment
choice_c: A fact known exclusively to the licensee's firm
choice_d: A condition or occurrence recognized by a competent licensee as significantly affecting the property's value, structural integrity, or presenting a health risk, or information indicating a party is unable to meet contractual obligations
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'adverse fact' as a condition or occurrence recognized by a competent licensee as significantly affecting the value, structural integrity, or safety/health aspects of the property, or as information that indicates a party is unable to meet the party's obligations in a transaction.

question: Per REEB 24.02, a "builder" is defined as what?
choice_a: Any person engaged in the business of constructing homes without a buyer under contract, or constructing homes under a contract with the buyer
choice_b: Only a person licensed as a general contractor by the state
choice_c: Only a corporation, never an individual
choice_d: Any person who has ever performed home repairs
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'builder' as any person engaged in the business of constructing homes without a buyer under contract or constructing homes under a contract with the buyer.

question: Per REEB 24.02, a "buyer's firm" is defined as what?
choice_a: Any firm that has ever represented a buyer, even in a prior transaction
choice_b: A firm that has an agency agreement with a buyer
choice_c: A firm that only handles new-construction purchases
choice_d: The listing firm, once an offer is accepted
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'buyer's firm' simply as a firm who has an agency agreement with a buyer.

question: Per REEB 24.02, when are two or more corporations considered a "commonly controlled corporation"?
choice_a: When they share the same registered agent
choice_b: When they operate out of the same office building
choice_c: When identical persons own at least 80% of the voting power and shares in each corporation
choice_d: When they are both licensed real estate firms
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'commonly controlled corporation' as two or more corporations where identical persons own at least 80% of the voting power and shares in each corporation.

question: Per REEB 24.02, what does it mean for a person to have "effectively controlled" real estate?
choice_a: Holding record title to the real estate
choice_b: Merely having a listing contract on the real estate
choice_c: Having lived on the real estate for over one year
choice_d: Having the power or authority to cause transfer of an interest in real estate for oneself or another, but not including authority conferred merely by a real estate listing contract
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'effectively controlled' as having the power or authority to cause the transfer of an interest in real estate for oneself or another, but excludes the authority conferred by a real estate listing contract alone.

question: Per REEB 24.02, how is a "party" defined for purposes of chapter REEB 24?
choice_a: A person seeking to engage in a transaction
choice_b: Only a person who has signed a contract
choice_c: Only a licensee's client
choice_d: Only the buyer, never the seller
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'party' as a person seeking to engage in a transaction, a broad definition covering both clients and customers.

question: Per REEB 24.02, a "principal firm" is defined as what?
choice_a: The largest firm in a given market
choice_b: A firm that engages a subagent to provide brokerage services in a transaction
choice_c: A firm whose broker has the most years of licensure
choice_d: Any firm holding an exclusive listing
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'principal firm' as a firm that engages a subagent to provide brokerage services in a transaction.

question: Per REEB 24.02, who qualifies as a "qualified third party" whose inspection or investigation results a licensee may rely upon?
choice_a: Only a person licensed as a professional home inspector
choice_b: Any friend or family member of the licensee
choice_c: A federal, state, or local governmental agency, or a person reasonably believed to possess inspection expertise
choice_d: Only another real estate licensee
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'qualified third party' as a federal, state, or local governmental agency, or a person reasonably believed by the licensee to possess the necessary skill, training, and experience to conduct the inspection or investigation.

question: Per REEB 24.02, a "secured lender" is defined as what?
choice_a: Any bank operating a branch in Wisconsin
choice_b: Only a licensed mortgage broker
choice_c: A party who has pre-approved financing for any transaction
choice_d: An individual or organization originating a loan in a transaction that is secured by real estate or by the assets of a business or business opportunity
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'secured lender' as an individual or organization originating a loan in a real estate or business opportunity transaction that is secured by real estate or by the assets of a business or business opportunity.

question: Per REEB 24.02, "real estate practice" is defined as what?
choice_a: Engaging in conduct that requires a license under ch. 452
choice_b: Only listing property for sale
choice_c: Only closing transactions as a title agent
choice_d: Any activity performed inside a real estate office
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'real estate practice' as engaging in conduct that requires a license under ch. 452, Stats.

question: Per REEB 24.02, a "right of first refusal" is defined as what?
choice_a: The right of a seller to reject the first offer received
choice_b: The right of a person to have the first opportunity to purchase or lease real property
choice_c: The right of a licensee to be the first to show a new listing
choice_d: The right of a buyer to a full refund of earnest money
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'right of first refusal' as the right of a person to have the first opportunity to purchase or lease real property.

question: Per REEB 24.02, a "written proposal" includes what range of documents?
choice_a: Only the final signed offer to purchase
choice_b: Only documents notarized by a licensed notary
choice_c: Any written document provided by one party to another during a transaction, including notices, offers, counteroffers, options, exchanges, rental agreements, and amendments
choice_d: Only documents prepared by an attorney
explanation: REEB 24.02 defines 'written proposal' broadly to include any written document provided by one party to another during the course of a transaction, including notices, offers, counteroffers, options, exchanges, rental agreements, and amendments.

question: Per REEB 24.03(2)(b), licensees have a general duty to act to protect the public against what?
choice_a: Rising interest rates
choice_b: Competing firms' marketing efforts
choice_c: Fluctuations in the broader housing market
choice_d: Fraud, misrepresentation, and unethical practices
explanation: REEB 24.03(2)(b) states that licensees shall act to protect the public against fraud, misrepresentation, and unethical practices.

question: Per REEB 24.03(2)(c), a licensee shall be knowledgeable regarding what, and shall assist, guide, and advise the parties on these factors?
choice_a: Laws, public policies, and current market conditions on real estate matters
choice_b: The personal financial history of each party
choice_c: Every other licensee's commission structure in the local market
choice_d: The internal operations of competing brokerages
explanation: REEB 24.03(2)(c) requires a licensee to be knowledgeable regarding laws, public policies, and current market conditions on real estate matters, and to assist, guide, and advise the parties on these factors.

question: Per REEB 24.07(2), separate from the pre-listing inspection duty, what general disclosure obligation applies whenever a licensee engages in real estate practice?
choice_a: The licensee must disclose facts only if a party specifically asks about them in writing
choice_b: The licensee may not exaggerate or misrepresent facts, and shall disclose to each party, in writing and in a timely fashion, all material adverse facts the licensee knows that the party does not know or cannot discover through reasonably vigilant observation
choice_c: The licensee has no disclosure duty once the listing contract is signed
choice_d: The licensee must disclose facts only to the licensee's own client, never to the other party
explanation: REEB 24.07(2) provides that a licensee may not exaggerate or misrepresent facts, and shall disclose to each party, in writing and in a timely fashion, all material adverse facts that the licensee knows and that the party does not know or cannot discover through reasonably vigilant observation.

question: Per REEB 24.07(4), if a licensee becomes aware that a party has not disclosed the party's entire agreement regarding the transaction to that party's secured lender, what must the licensee do?
choice_a: Say nothing, since it is a private matter between the party and the lender
choice_b: Refuse to close the transaction until the lender is paid off
choice_c: Disclose this fact, in writing and in a timely manner, to the party's secured lender
choice_d: Report the party to the board for lender fraud
explanation: REEB 24.07(4) requires a licensee who becomes aware that a party has not disclosed the party's entire agreement regarding the transaction to that party's secured lender to disclose this fact, in writing and in a timely manner, to the secured lender.

question: Per REEB 24.07(6), if a licensee's inspection reveals facts materially inconsistent with the seller's statements or a third party's report, what must the licensee do?
choice_a: Ignore the inconsistency if the seller's statement was made in good faith
choice_b: Wait until the buyer raises the issue before saying anything
choice_c: Resolve the inconsistency personally before disclosing anything
choice_d: Disclose the inconsistency in writing and in a timely manner to the parties
explanation: REEB 24.07(6) requires that if a licensee's reasonably competent and diligent inspection reveals facts materially inconsistent with or contradictory to the seller's statements or a third party's inspection/investigation report, the inconsistency must be disclosed in writing and in a timely manner to the parties.

question: Per REEB 24.07(7), what are licensees prohibited from doing regarding other licensees or their listings?
choice_a: Knowingly giving false information about another licensee or property listed with another licensee
choice_b: Showing a property listed with another firm
choice_c: Commenting on a competing listing's price to a client, if the comment is accurate
choice_d: Contacting another licensee to arrange a showing
explanation: REEB 24.07(7) states that licensees shall not knowingly give false information about another licensee or about property listed with another licensee.

question: Per REEB 24.13(1), when may a licensee refuse to draft or submit a written proposal?
choice_a: Whenever the licensee personally disagrees with the proposed price
choice_b: Only if the terms of the proposal would be contrary to specific written instructions of the other party
choice_c: Whenever the proposal is submitted after 5:00 p.m.
choice_d: A licensee may never refuse to draft or submit a written proposal, under any circumstance
explanation: REEB 24.13(1) prohibits licensees from refusing to draft or submit any written proposal unless the terms of the written proposal would be contrary to specific written instructions of the other party.

question: Per REEB 24.13(2), a listing firm must permit access to a listed property for showing purposes to whom, and under what condition?
choice_a: Only buyers who are pre-approved for financing
choice_b: Only buyers represented by a licensee from the same firm
choice_c: All buyers and persons assisting or advising buyers, without unreasonable delay, unless access is contrary to the seller's specific written instructions
choice_d: Only during the listing firm's normal office hours
explanation: REEB 24.13(2) requires listing firms to permit access to listed property for showing purposes, without unreasonable delay, to all buyers and persons assisting or advising buyers, unless access is contrary to the seller's specific written instructions.

question: Per REEB 24.13(3)(a), how must a licensee present written proposals to clients and customers?
choice_a: In whatever manner the licensee's firm's internal policy dictates, with no state-level standard
choice_b: Only in person, never electronically
choice_c: Only after obtaining the other party's consent to the presentation format
choice_d: In an objective and unbiased manner, informing them of the advantages and disadvantages of all submitted proposals
explanation: REEB 24.13(3)(a) requires licensees to present all written proposals in an objective and unbiased manner, informing their clients and customers of the advantages and disadvantages of all submitted written proposals.

question: Per REEB 24.13(3)(c), a licensee must promptly present all written proposals received, and may not withhold a later proposal pending action on an earlier one, except when?
choice_a: Presentation would be contrary to specific written instructions from the licensee's client or customer
choice_b: The later proposal is for a lower price than the earlier one
choice_c: The licensee believes the earlier proposal will be accepted first
choice_d: More than three proposals have already been presented
explanation: REEB 24.13(3)(c) requires prompt presentation of all written proposals received, and prohibits withholding a proposal pending action on a previously presented one, unless presentation would be contrary to specific written instructions from the licensee's client or customer.

question: Per REEB 24.13(4), what must a licensee do regarding the outcome of a submitted written proposal, and what must be provided immediately upon request?
choice_a: Nothing further is required once the proposal is presented
choice_b: Promptly inform clients/customers whether a proposal was accepted, rejected, or countered, and immediately provide a written statement with the date and time of presentation, or of rejection/expiration, when requested by the other party or that party's firm
choice_c: Notify only the licensee's own broker, not the client
choice_d: Wait until closing to disclose whether the proposal was accepted
explanation: REEB 24.13(4) requires licensees to promptly inform their clients and customers whether a written proposal was accepted, rejected, or countered, and to immediately provide a written statement of presentation date/time, or rejection/expiration date/time, when requested by the other party's firm.

question: Per REEB 24.17(2), on what basis may the board discipline a licensee relating to a criminal matter?
choice_a: An arrest alone, even without any conviction
choice_b: A conviction for any offense whatsoever, regardless of its relation to real estate
choice_c: A conviction of any crime, the circumstances of which substantially relate to the practice of real estate
choice_d: A civil judgment only, never a criminal conviction
explanation: REEB 24.17(2) allows the board to discipline a licensee on the basis of a conviction of any crime, the circumstances of which substantially relate to the practice of real estate.

question: Per REEB 24.17(2m), the board may revoke a license based on a felony conviction that bars licensure under which statute?
choice_a: Section 452.01(2)
choice_b: Section 452.03
choice_c: Section 452.132
choice_d: Section 452.25(1)(a)
explanation: REEB 24.17(2m) ties board revocation authority to felony convictions that bar an individual from receiving an initial license under s. 452.25(1)(a).
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code REEB 24.17(2m); Wis. Stat. 452.25(1)(a)

question: Per REEB 24.17(3), licensees may not violate, or aid or abet the violation of, what, in addition to ch. 452?
choice_a: Any provisions, terms, or conditions of chs. REEB 11 to 25, or any order of the board
choice_b: Any provision of federal tax law
choice_c: Only rules adopted after the licensee's initial licensure date
choice_d: Only rules specifically labeled as mandatory
explanation: REEB 24.17(3) prohibits licensees from violating, or aiding or abetting the violation of, any provisions or terms or conditions of, ch. 452, Stats., chs. REEB 11 to 25, or any order of the board.

question: Per REEB 24.17(4), a licensee may not render services under what condition?
choice_a: While working more than 40 hours in a week
choice_b: While the licensee's ability to competently perform duties is impaired by mental or emotional disorder, drugs, or alcohol
choice_c: While representing more than one client simultaneously
choice_d: While using a personal cell phone for business calls
explanation: REEB 24.17(4) prohibits licensees from rendering services while the licensee's ability to competently perform duties is impaired by mental or emotional disorder, drugs, or alcohol.
